new_jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer - Digital Platform and AWS (260807)

**Our Commitment to You**  
  
At Consumer Cellular, recruiting is human. Every application is reviewed by a real member of our Talent Acquisition team because we believe the people behind the résumé matter just as much as what's on it.  
  
All official communication from Consumer Cellular will come from a @consumercellular.com email address or through our verified texting platform, which will only be used to schedule interviews. We will never ask for personal and financial information during the recruiting process. If you receive outreach that doesn't match these criteria, please do not engage and feel free to verify directly at talentacquisition@consumercellular.com.

**Job Summary**  
Consumer Cellular is building a new cloud-native platform on Amazon Web Services, and we are hiring Senior Software Engineers to build the services that run on it.

This is a hands-on product engineering role. You will design and ship the APIs and event-driven services behind our customer-facing digital experiences- account management, activation, billing, and self-service - using a serverless-first architecture on AWS. You will work in Python and TypeScript, make substantive data modeling decisions across several purpose-built data stores, and own your services in production.

Two things make this a compelling time to join. The platform is new, so the patterns are not all set yet and your design decisions will outlive your first year. And we are migrating a large group of experienced colleagues onto it, so Senior Engineers here have real influence on how the whole organization builds- not only on their own backlog.

We serve millions of customers who depend on us for something that matters staying connected to the people they care about. Our customer base skews older than the industry average, which makes clarity, reliability, and accessibility engineering requirements rather than afterthoughts. If you like the idea of your work being judged by whether it works for people who are not power users, you will fit in well here.

**You will need to reside within 50 miles of our Corporate Headquarters in Scottsdale, AZ as this role has the option of hybrid or onsite.**

**Responsibilities**

* **Design and build production services.** Develop serverless APIs and event-driven workflows using AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and Amazon EventBridge, written in Python and Node/TypeScript.
* **Make and data modeling decisions.** We use several data stores deliberately: Amazon DynamoDB, Aurora DSQL, Amazon DocumentDB, and Amazon S3. You will select between them based on access patterns, and you will be expected to explain why.
* **Own what you ship.** Instrument your services, build the dashboards and alarms, author the runbooks, and participate in an on-call rotation for the services your team owns.
* **Build for failure.** Asynchronous systems fail in ways request/response systems do not. You will design for retries, idempotency, duplicate delivery, and partial failure as a matter of course.
* **Work in a modern delivery pipeline.** GitHub and GitHub Actions, OIDC-federated deployments, infrastructure as code, Ansible for configuration management, and service-to-service connectivity via Amazon VPC Lattice.
* **Raise the bar through review.** Provide thorough, constructive, and useful code and design review. A meaningful share of your impact in this role shows up in other people’s work.
* **Support colleague migration.** Pair with engineers moving onto the platform from our existing stack, and help turn what you learn into documentation and reusable patterns. We have built a structured enablement program, and Senior Engineers are central to it.
* **Contribute to platform standards.** Logging conventions, error handling, IAM patterns, repository structure, and data store selection guidance.

**Qualifications (Education, Experience, Skills)**

**Required**
------------

* Five or more years building and operating backend services in production. We care about depth of ownership rather than the number itself; if you have shipped and supported real systems that people depended on, tell us about it.
* **Strong proficiency in Python or TypeScript/Node**, and willingness to work in both. Most of our engineers arrive strong in one.
* **Hands-on AWS experience**, including a working understanding of IAM, networking fundamentals, and at least one managed AWS data service.
* Experience designing REST APIs and integrating distributed systems.
* Practical experience with relational data modeling and SQL, including how schema choices affect performance.
* Comfort with Git-based workflows and CI/CD, and an established habit of automated testing.
* Demonstrated debugging skill in distributed systems — you can work a problem from logs, metrics, and traces rather than by guessing.
* Clear written communication. Design documents, decision records, and review comments are a substantial part of this job.

**Strongly Preferred**
----------------------

* **Production serverless experience** — AWS Lambda or equivalent, including the operational realities that come with it: cold starts, concurrency limits, timeouts, and execution-role scoping.
* **Production event-driven architecture experience** — EventBridge, Kafka, SNS/SQS, or similar, including idempotency and dead-letter handling.
* **NoSQL data modeling**, particularly DynamoDB single-table design and access-pattern-first modeling.
* **Migration or modernization experience**, moving workloads from traditional infrastructure to cloud-native architectures.
* Infrastructure as code (CloudFormation, CDK, SAM, or Ansible)
* Observability practice: structured logging, distributed tracing, alarm design, and service level objectives.
* **Cost-aware engineering** — you consider what a design costs to run, not only whether it works.

**Preferred**
-------------

* Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, LiteLLM, or comparable LLM applica

At SiFly, we’re building a new category of aircraft: vertical-takeoff, long-endurance drones that deliver helicopter-level performance at drone economics. We merge aerial robotics, perception, and onboard intelligence to cut complexity and minimize human intervention, and our unique approach to communications and networking unlocks remote operations from day one. It’s an ambitious mission, and we’re a small team that moves fast.

We are looking for a highly capable engineer who can contribute across embedded development, real-time processing, and system integration. * **Work in the field.** Collaborate closely with the team to design architecture, test on real aircraft, and iterate quickly on what you learn there.

**Embedded Linux Engineer — Networking & Connectivity**

**EMBEDDED PLATFORM · FULL TIME · ON-SITE — SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA**

**About SiFly Aviation**
------------------------

At SiFly, we're building a new category of aircraft: vertical-takeoff, long-endurance drones that deliver helicopter-level performance at drone economics. After thousands of flight tests and years of engineering, our NDAA-compliant platform flies more than 2 hours in hover or 3 hours in forward flight on a single charge — matching the capability of traditional helicopters at a fraction of their cost and operational burden. We merge aerial robotics, perception, and onboard intelligence to cut complexity and minimize human intervention, and our unique approach to communications and networking unlocks remote operations from day one. It's an ambitious mission, and we're a small team that moves fast.

We are looking for a senior Embedded Linux Engineer to own connectivity on the aircraft: how a Q12 stays reachable over 5G, Wi-Fi 6, and Wi-Fi HaLow simultaneously, how traffic is routed and prioritized across those links as they degrade, and how video, telemetry, and command-and-control survive a handover mid-flight. Remote beyond-visual-line-of-sight operation is the product, and the network is what makes it possible. The picture is also wider than the aircraft alone: the same links and routing decisions span the DroneFi ground station and the pilot application, and you will own how they behave as one system.

This is a role with real ownership rather than a specification to implement. You will own our Dynamic Routing Engine — the service that decides, in flight, which link carries what — along with the link-management daemons, the secure overlay back to our cloud, and the test rigs that prove any of it works. The engine is led part-time today; ownership of it transfers to you as you onboard — and with it, the role of primary technical guide for DroneFi development, supported by the senior architect who owns our low-level networking foundations. We are hiring two Embedded Linux Engineers with deliberately different centres of gravity: you own connectivity and routing, while a counterpart works broadly across the platform — platform services, integration, and new platform capabilities — alongside the senior engineers who already cover BSP, boot, and the update pipeline. You will work closely together.

**The Role**
------------

You will own the networking stack on the aircraft and the software that manages it: multi-link connectivity across cellular, Wi-Fi 6, and Wi-Fi HaLow, the Dynamic Routing Engine that selects and blends those links, traffic policy and QoS that keeps command-and-control alive when video wants all the bandwidth, the Tailscale mesh and TLS-secured paths back to our AWS backend, and the behaviour of MQTT, WebRTC video, and the MAVLink router under real loss and latency. Day to day that means writing services in C, C++, and Python on a Yocto-based platform, living in packet captures, and building the emulation and field-test setups that turn “it felt better” into a number. You own the connectivity picture in its totality: not just the Linux side, but partnering with the applications team so the software riding on these links is as resilient to degradation and handover as the network beneath it.

You will collaborate closely with the rest of the embedded platform team — your generalist counterpart and the engineers who cover BSP, boot, updates, and the low-level networking foundations — the firmware engineers who own the radios and supervisory MCUs, the part-time engineer who leads the Dynamic Routing Engine today and will hand it over to you, the applications and autonomy teams whose traffic you carry and whose resilience you help design, the cloud team on the other end of every link, and our hardware and RF engineers in Santa Clara — including on antenna placement and integration on the airframe.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Own the Dynamic Routing Engine.** Design, implement, and harden the service that chooses and blends links in flight — link metrics and scoring, switching policy and hysteresis, failover timing, and behaviour at the edge of coverage — and close out the open risks against it.
* **Make multi-link connectivity dependable.** Own the cellular, Wi-Fi 6, and Wi-Fi HaLow links end-to-end on the Linux side: modem management, association and roaming, bonding and make-before-break handover, and graceful degradation rather than a cliff edge.
* **Own routing and traffic policy.** Policy routing across multiple tables and interfaces, nftables, tc-based QoS and shaping, VLANs, bridges, and network namespaces — so command-and-control, video, and bulk transfer each get what they need on a link that is shrinking.
* **Keep video and telemetry alive under degradation.** Tune WebRTC (WHIP/WHEP) and RTP video, adaptive bitrate and congestion control, MQTT keepalive and reconnect behaviour, and MAVLink routing on lossy, high-latency links — and make reconnection invisible to the operator.
* **Make the applications resilient with you.** Own the contract between the network and everything riding on it: expose link state, quality, and bandwidth signals that applications can act on, and work with the applications team so onboard and ground-side software handles degradation, handover, and offline periods by design rather than by surprise.
* **Own the secure overlay.** The Tailscale/WireGuard mesh, TLS, per-aircraft identity and certificate provisioning, NAT traversal, and an addressing plan that still works when the fleet is an order of magnitude larger.
* **Instrument the network.** Per-link metrics for signal quality, latency, loss, jitter, and throughput; structured connectivity logging that makes a post-flight “why did the link drop” answerable from data rather than guesswork.

new_jobs.title: Embedded Flight Software Engineer
new_jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Proteus Space is a Los Angeles-based spacecraft technology company established to capitalize on a rapidly evolving space landscape and the urgent need to deliver resilient orbital capabilities to maintain and increase our national science and security interests. We combine serious space flight experience with an open minded, first-principles approach, leveraging advanced computational design and Industry 4.0 practices to deliver custom spacecraft and mission solutions with industry leading speed, precision, and reliability. We seek to enable every payload and mission with a fully custom, purpose-built spacecraft bus, designed and delivered using Proteus™, our patent-pending, automated computational design platform, with industry leading reliability.

**Role Description**

We are seeking an Embedded Flight Software Engineer with deep expertise in low-level embedded software, FPGA interfaces, drivers, and bootloader development to join our flight program team. This is a full-time, in-office role for an experienced professional with a proven track record of hands-on FSW development. In this role, you will design and implement low-level drivers, BSPs, and boot systems while managing memory architectures and FPGA hardware interfaces. You will bridge the gap between low-level hardware and high-level FSW logic, ensuring reliable spacecraft boot behavior, fail-safe recovery, and deterministic bus communications in space environments.

**Key Responsibilities**.

* Develop low-level C/C++ drivers, Board Support Packages (BSPs), and hardware interfaces for microcontrollers, FPGAs, and standard communication buses.
* Design and implement stage-1 and stage-2 bootloaders, robust boot behaviors, partition swapping logic, and fail-safe recovery modes.
* Architect memory management strategies across volatile and non-volatile memory (NOR/NAND Flash, SRAM, EEPROM) to preserve data integrity across reboots.
* Configure low-level communication protocols and bus interfaces (e.g., SPI, I2C, CAN, UART, SpaceWire, or PCIe) between compute units, peripherals, and payloads.
* Implement telemetry collection, time synchronization, and task scheduling within RTOS or embedded OS environments.
* Execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and debugging on flatsats using logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and FPGA emulator tools.
* Manage the codebase using modern version control systems and contribute to CI/CD workflows for automated testing and continuous integration.
* Execute comprehensive test campaigns on testbeds and flight units to verify software performance under flight-like conditions.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate subsystems with the spacecraft main compute element.
* Ensure compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.
* Document design processes, test results, and system performance.
* Provide technical guidance on FSW architectures to fellow engineers, fostering a culture of excellence and innovation.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or advanced degree in computer science, aerospace engineering, or similar field.
* 5+ years of embedded software engineering experience, with exposure to low-level driver development, hardware integration, or bootloaders.
* Strong proficiency in C, C++, embedded Linux, and Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS).
* Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git) and automated testing/CI workflows.
* Strong ability to collaborate effectively in a dynamic environment while maintaining a positive and professional attitude.
* Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
* Must possess or be willing and eligible to obtain a United States Department of Defense Top Secret security clearance.

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Experience writing custom drivers for FPGA logic blocks or hardware interfaces (such as I2C, CAN, SPI, UART, or SpaceWire).
* Experience with hardware-level communication protocols and hardware/software integration.
* Experience working in clean room environments and adhering to ESD protocols.
* Demonstrated experience with custom bootloader design, memory controller drivers, Flash file systems, and image verification/recovery techniques.

**Salary Range:** $130,000 - $180,000 per year. Final compensation is based on experience, education and qualifications.

**Benefits**

Proteus Space offers comprehensive benefits including paid medical healthcare for employees, flexible vacation policy, sick days, 401k matching option, pregnancy leave, family leave, holiday pay, military service leave, dental care, vision care and other benefits.

**Equal Opportunity**

Proteus is committed to providing equal employment opportunities regardless of an applicant's age, disability, sex, race, religion, gender, national origin, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic. The Company will provide reasonable accommodations to an applicant with a disability or religious belief in or to enable the applicant to apply for the position.

NVIDIA is powering the next generation of AI computing, and our firmware team helps turn groundbreaking technology into production datacenters. We are looking for a Senior SBIOS Firmware Engineer to help customers bring NVIDIA platforms to life—from initial system bring-up and reference platform qualification through deployment at scale. You will help build the infrastructure that powers AI while using AI tools to accelerate development, solve complex system problems, and improve how we deliver reliable platforms to customers.

* Supporting reference platforms across the product lifecycle, establishing validated firmware configurations, documenting platform behavior, and making solutions reusable across customer designs.
* Investigating complex issues across firmware, hardware, BMC, and operating system boundaries, including boot, hardware initialization, PCIe enumeration, memory configuration, performance, and reliability.
* Partnering with hardware, firmware, software, validation, and customer engineering teams to drive issues from reproduction and root cause analysis through verified fixes and customer adoption.
* Using AI-assisted development, debugging, and automation to analyze logs, accelerate root cause investigation, improve test coverage, and turn recurring support problems into scalable engineering solutions.
* Developing diagnostic tools, automated tests, and technical guidance that improve platform readiness and help customers deploy and operate systems successfully.
Communicating technical findings, risks, and resolution plans clearly to internal teams and external partners.  

  

**What we need to see:**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field—or equivalent experience—with 5+ years of relevant experience.
* Strong experience developing and debugging System BIOS/UEFI firmware on ARM or x86 server platforms, including familiarity with EDK II architecture.
* Solid understanding of server architecture, including processor initialization, memory systems, PCIe, interrupts, boot flows, and interactions among SBIOS, BMC, and the operating system.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex system issues using firmware logs, operating system diagnostics, hardware interfaces, and structured experiments.
* Experience supporting server bring-up, platform qualification, or customer deployment, with ownership of technical issues through resolution.
* Strong C programming skills and experience using Python or shell scripting to build diagnostic tools and automate engineering workflows.
* Hands-on experience applying AI tools to software development, debugging, testing, or technical analysis, with the engineering judgment to independently verify generated code and conclusions.
* Understanding of server reliability, availability, and serviceability (RAS), firmware security, and the requirements of production datacenter environments.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate directly with customers and partners and drive progress across global engineering teams.  

  

**Ways to stand out from the crowd:**

* Proven experience enabling customer deployments of NVIDIA CPU or GPU server platforms, from early bring-up through production.
* Deep expertise in ARM server architecture, UEFI, ACPI, SMBIOS, or firmware interfaces with Linux.
* Experience debugging issues that span SBIOS, BMC, and platform management interfaces such as IPMI, MCTP, and PLDM.
* A track record of building AI-assisted engineering workflows that measurably improve debugging speed, software quality, or customer support efficiency.
Experience turning reference platform designs and lessons from customer deployments into reusable tools, documentation, and validation coverage.  

  

NVIDIA brings together talented engineers to solve some of computing’s most challenging problems. If you enjoy working directly with customers, digging into complex systems, and using AI to improve how engineering gets done, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 152,000 USD - 241,500 USD for Level 3, and 184,000 USD - 287,500 USD for Level 4.

* Experience with performing and generating tools/code for spacecraft propulsion related subsystem analyses, such as flow-pressure drop and test data reduction.
* Ability to perform first-order (hand calculation) and excel-level calculations.
* Capable of reporting and presenting complex analytical results clearly to multi-disciplinary teams.
* Familiarity with developing, supporting and conducting propulsion subsystem ground testing.

* Implement and deploy state-of-the-art learning-based manipulation policies to achieve reliable, world-class performance on real-world tasks with physical hardware.
* Adapt and improve policies for new tasks and hardware using post-training methods such as RL fine-tuning, policy distillation, and interactive imitation learning (e.g., DAgger).
* Build and maintain the data pipelines that support post-training, including teleoperation and demonstration collection, retargeting, dataset aggregation, and curation.
* Drive the development cycle from simulation and offline evaluation to robustly transferring and fine-tuning policies on the robot.
* Develop visuomotor policies for grasping, in-hand manipulation, and whole-arm manipulation, with reliable, low-latency execution on hardware.
* Define evaluation metrics and regression tests for policy performance in simulation and on hardware, and use the results to guide technical decisions.
* Collaborate closely with the simulation, data, hardware, and systems teams to diagnose system-level issues and co-develop solutions.
* Maintain high standards for the codebase through testing, documentation, and peer code reviews.
  

**SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS**

**Technical Skills (Must-Have)**

* **Manipulation:** Strong experience in robotic manipulation, including grasping, in-hand or whole-arm control, and high-DOF motion, with a track record of hardware deployment.
* **Learning-Based Control:** Hands-on experience training and debugging learned policies, including post-training methods such as RL fine-tuning, distillation, and imitation learning (e.g., DAgger).
* **Software Engineering:** Proficiency in Python, C++, and PyTorch or JAX, with experience building real-time robotic software stacks.
* **Data & Evaluation:** Experience working with demonstration and teleoperation data, and building evaluation pipelines for learned policies.

**Good to Have**

* **Simulation Environments:** Experience with physics engines such as IsaacSim, MuJoCo, or Drake for policy training and validation.
* **Generalist Policies:** Experience adapting large, general-purpose manipulation policies to specific tasks and embodiments.
* **Teleoperation:** Experience with VR/haptic interfaces and retargeting algorithms for human-in-the-loop control.
* **Tactile Sensing:** Experience integrating tactile/haptic feedback into manipulation pipelines.
* **Computer Vision:** Familiarity with 6D pose estimation, point cloud processing, or visual-servoing.

  

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* An MS with 3+ years of relevant experience, or a recent PhD, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
* Relevant experience specifically focused on learning-based manipulation or a closely related area.
* A proven track record of taking learned policies from a research/simulation environment and successfully deploying them on physical hardware.

  

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
* Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times
* Vision to read printed materials and a computer screen
* Hearing and speech to communicate

The annual salary range is $180,000 - $240,000

new_jobs.description:
### **Overview**

Mainspring Energy is seeking a highly skilled **Sr. Staff Controls Software Engineer** to architect, develop, and deploy industrial-grade Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI) and SCADA systems for our Linear Generator sites. As a senior individual contributor and technical lead, you will define the architecture for modernizing our operator interfaces using Ignition, building scalable, site-agnostic UI frameworks, and implementing robust industrial communication pipelines using OPC UA, Modbus, and related protocols. You will bridge hardware controls, site telemetry, and operator visualization to deliver intuitive, reliable, and secure control interfaces across commercial, microgrid, and utility-scale deployments.

### **Responsibilities**

* **Ignition HMI Development:** Lead the design, architecture, and deployment of commercial-grade operator interfaces standardized on the Ignition SCADA platform.
* **Site-Agnostic UI Architecture:** Build dynamic, site-agnostic HMI screens and tag structures that seamlessly scale across diverse power plant configurations, skids, and high generator counts.
* **Protocol & Telemetry Integration:** Implement robust communication interfaces and telemetry pipelines utilizing OPC-UA, Modbus, and SunSpec for real-time SCADA data exposure and third-party integration.
* **Alarming & Diagnostics:** Develop comprehensive alarm management, system of events logging, and diagnostic dashboards for deep visibility into site hardware and network status.
* **Testing & Validation:** Own the testing lifecycle for new features, including unit testing, integration testing, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) validation to ensure site safety logic and grid compliance.
* **DER Integration:** Implement strategies for integrating Mainspring technology into Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS) and complex microgrid environments.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** Work with Product, Controls and Hardware teams to translate utility requirements and interconnection standards into functional software specifications.

### **Qualifications**

* **Industry Experience:** 12+ years of hands-on experience in **commercial power generation**, industrial automation, manufacturing or utility-scale energy projects.
* **HMI & SCADA Expertise:** Deep hands-on experience building complex industrial HMI/SCADA systems, with demonstrated mastery of the **Ignition** platform (Perspective/Vision modules, UDTs, Tag Historian) and industrial communication protocols, specifically **OPC-UA**, Modbus TCP/RTU, and SunSpec, alongside relational database integration (e.g., PostgreSQL).
* **Software Architecture & Scalability:** Proven experience defining industrial software architecture, leading technical decisions, and delivering reusable, site-agnostic HMI/SCADA platforms from design through deployment.
* **Grid Interconnection Standards:** Experience with grid interconnection standards (e.g., IEEE 1547, UL 1741).
* **Cybersecurity Frameworks:** Knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks for industrial control systems (e.g., NERC CIP).
* **Technical Communication:** Ability to create clear technical documentation and system diagrams that bridge the gap between industrial hardware and modern software.

This position is **onsite** at our **Menlo Park HQ**. The salary will be adjusted to reflect local market conditions based on employee location as well as the experience of the employee. Along with base salary, Mainspring offers pre-IPO company equity through Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) + benefits.

**What to Expect**

Tesla’s mission is to accelerate the world’s transition to sustainable energy. That mission depends on parts that switch, actuate, and isolate at high voltage, high current, and high cadence.

The Supplier Industrialization Engineer (SIE) for Electromechanical and Electromagnetic Devices is the manufacturing owner for this commodity. You sit between Design, Purchasing, and the supplier. You are the resident process expert, the NPI lead at the factory, and the person who does not accept “the line has always run this way.”

You will industrialize contactors, relays, solenoids, actuators, pyro disconnects, switches, and small electromagnetic machines from first samples through mass production. You will spend real time on supplier floors such as welding cells, winding lines, plating, overmold, and end-of-line test. You will make on-the-spot decisions that protect Tesla’s launch and the customer.

The pace is high. The work is first principles, data, and process control, not slideware.

 **What You'll Do**

* Own industrialization of electromechanical and electromagnetic devices from advanced development through PPAP / production part approval and stable mass production — including high-voltage contactors and relays, solenoids, actuators, pyro disconnects, switches, small motors, and related electromagnetic assemblies
* Plan, organize, and execute supplier process development: stamping and forming of magnetic circuits and contact systems; coil winding and termination; resistance / laser welding; plating; overmolding and potting; hermetic sealing; and final functional test
* Lead Design for Manufacturability (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) with Tesla Design, Reliability, and the supplier. Close air-gap, contact-force, weld, creepage/clearance, and tolerance stack-up issues before tooling kickoff

* Audit suppliers against IATF 16949, VDA 6.3, and Tesla process requirements. Identify gaps in process control, change management, and sub-tier (contacts, magnets, coils, plastics, platings) and close them with the supplier
* Lead debug when yield, reliability, or delivery breaks. Run structured problem solving (8D, FTA, DOE, Ishikawa) and implement permanent countermeasure. Travel to supplier sites and Tesla factories and make technical decisions on the floor
* Translate Tesla application conditions (inrush, inductive load, vibration, thermal cycling, salt, HV isolation) into supplier process windows and validation plans (ISO 16750, LV 124 / VW 80000, AEC-Q200, IEC / UL where applicable)
* Partner with Purchasing, Quality, NPI, and Manufacturing to hit cost, quality (PPM), and delivery. Challenge the supplier on cycle time, scrap, automation, and material utilization — first principles, not tradition

  
**What You'll Bring**

* Degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Manufacturing, or Materials Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 3+ years industrializing, manufacturing, or qualifying electromechanical or electromagnetic devices (contactors, relays, solenoids, actuators, motors, switches, or similar). Automotive, industrial power, or high-reliability electronics preferred
* Hands-on fluency with the processes that actually make these parts: coil winding, contact welding, magnetic circuit stamping, plating, overmold, potting, hermetic seal, and functional test
* Working knowledge of contact physics (arcing, bounce, welding, material transfer), electromagnetic actuation (force vs. air gap, coil heating, residual magnetism), and insulation / creepage at high voltage
* Proven ownership of APQP / PPAP (or equivalent), PFMEA, control plans, MSA, SPC, and process capability (Cpk) on electrical and mechanical special characteristics
* Ability to read drawings, GD&T, and electrical specifications; to challenge a datasheet; and to write a clear process or test requirement
* Structured problem solving (8D, FTA, DOE, 5-Why) and comfort with data (Excel required; JMP, Minitab, or Python a plus)
* Experience auditing manufacturing quality systems (IATF 16949, VDA 6.3, ISO 9001) and driving sub-tier control
* Clear, direct communication with suppliers and internal engineering — written and on the factory floor. You influence without hiding behind process theater
* Preferred: high-voltage contactor / pyro-fuse / traction-inverter or energy-product component experience; Six Sigma / CQE; Mandarin, German, Korean, or Japanese

#### **Benefits**

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:

* Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction

new_jobs.title: Data Platform Engineer
new_jobs.description:
We are a high-growth company transforming how businesses operate by integrating AI, IoT, and cloud-native services into scalable, real-time platforms. As a Platform Data Engineer, you’ll play a critical role in building and maintaining the data infrastructure that powers our products, services, and insights.  
  
You’ll join a multidisciplinary team focused on ingesting, processing, and managing massive streams of sensor and operational data across a wide array of devices—from drones and robots to industrial systems and smart environments.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Design, build, and maintain scalable, reliable, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines for structured and semi-structured data.
* Implement robust and secure data lake and SQL-based storage architectures optimized for performance and cost.
* Develop and maintain internal tools and frameworks for data ingestion using Python, Golang, and SQL.
* Build and maintain inference pipelines to support model serving and near real time prediction workflows
* Develop and maintain internal tools and deployment processes to support ML development workflow , including experimentation, testing, deployment and monitoring.
* Collaborate cross-functionally with Cloud, Edge, Product, and AI teams to define data contracts, schemas, and retention policies.
* Use AWS cloud infrastructure (including Argo Workflows, S3, Lambda, Glue, Kinesis, Athena, and RDS) to support end-to-end data workflows.
* Employ Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) practices using Terraform to manage data platform infrastructure.
* Monitor data pipelines for quality, latency, and failures using tools such as CloudWatch, SumoLogic, or DataDog.
* Build and maintain ingestion pipelines that land curated sensor and operational data into Delta tables on Databricks to support ML experimentation and model training.
* Continuously optimize storage, partitioning, and query performance across large-scale datasets.
* Participate in architecture reviews and ensure the platform adheres to security, compliance, and best practice standards.

**Skills and Qualifications**

* 5+ years of professional experience in software engineering or data engineering.
* Strong programming skills in Python and Golang.
* Deep understanding of SQL and modern data lake architectures (e.g., using Parquet, Iceberg, or Delta Lake).
* Hands-on experience with AWS services including but not limited to: S3, Lambda, Glue, Kinesis, Athena, and RDS.
* Proficiency with Terraform for automating infrastructure deployment and management.
* Hands-on experience with Databricks for ML workflows: MLflow experiment tracking and model registry, Model Serving, and building training datasets in Delta Lake (PySpark/Spark SQL).
* Experience working with real-time or batch data ingestion at scale, and designing fault-tolerant ETL/ELT pipelines.
* Familiarity with DVC for dataset versioning and management.
* Familiarity with event-driven architectures and messaging systems like Kafka or Kinesis.
* Strong debugging and optimization skills across cloud, network, and application layers.
* Excellent collaboration, communication, and documentation skills.

**Bonus Points**

* Experience working with time-series or IoT sensor data at industrial scale.
* Exposure to gRPC and protobuf-based data contracts.
* Experience supporting ML pipelines and feature stores.
* Working knowledge of Kubernetes concepts.
* Databricks Machine Learning certification (Professional)
* Prior startup experience and/or comfort working in fast-paced, iterative environments.

2. Develop, validate, and optimize practical computer vision and image-processing algorithms for object detection, segmentation, feature extraction, alignment, identification, measurement, and defect inspection.

3. Design maintainable software components, interfaces, and architecture using object-oriented principles; independently own complex features and make sound technical design decisions.

4. Integrate machine vision software with automated equipment and imaging systems; apply machine learning techniques when appropriate, rather than as a primary requirement.

Practical development of computer vision/image-processing algorithms using OpenCV or equivalent libraries, including techniques such as segmentation, feature extraction, object detection, pattern matching, alignment, or measurement. **Who we are**

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We're changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don't just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

  

**About the role**

The QC Technician is the last check between our electronics and the field. You will flash firmware onto circuit boards every day, run functional tests, and make sure every board that leaves the bench is correctly programmed, traceable, and working.

This is a hands-on, bench-based role on the hardware production team. You will work closely with hardware and firmware engineers, follow documented procedures, and flag anything that looks off before it reaches a vehicle.

  

**What you'll do**

* Flash bootloaders, firmware, and configuration files onto PCBs and modules using programming fixtures, JTAG/SWD debuggers, USB/serial tools, and in-house scripts.
* Confirm the correct firmware version and configuration is loaded on every board, matched to the build order, and run batch flashing efficiently while keeping error rates near zero.
* Run functional and power-on tests after flashing, following test procedures and checklists; visually inspect boards for physical defects such as damaged components, solder issues, bent pins, and connector damage.
* Use multimeters, power supplies, and basic test equipment to check voltages and continuity.
* Separate passing and failing units, and tag failures clearly for engineering review. Write clear failure reports with symptoms, steps taken, and photos where useful.
* Log serial numbers, firmware versions, test results, and failures in our tracking system or spreadsheets, label boards and keep inventory of programmed, tested, and failed units accurate.
* Do first-level troubleshooting on failed flashes and tests: re-seat connections, check cables, retry, and swap fixtures–escalate recurring or unexplained failures to hardware and firmware engineers with enough detail to act on.

* Help keep work instructions and checklists up to date as firmware and hardware change, and support new product introductions and engineering builds when needed.

* High school diploma or equivalent; technical certificate or associate degree in electronics or a related field is a plus.
* 3+ year of hands-on experience in electronics manufacturing, test, QC, or a similar bench role.
* Comfortable handling PCBs and small components with ESD-safe practices.
* Basic use of a multimeter and bench power supply.
* Comfortable on a linux computer: running programs or scripts from instructions, using a command line at an intermediate level, and entering data accurately in spreadsheets or tracking tools.
* Able to follow written procedures exactly and recognize when something doesn't match them, clear written and verbal communication for logging results and reporting failures.
* Reliable, consistent, and comfortable with repetitive, high-volume work.
* Background in automotive, robotics, or heavy equipment electronics preferred.
* IPC-A-610 or IPC J-STD-001 certification, or working knowledge of PCB workmanship standards preferred.
* Experience flashing microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, NXP, or similar) with tools such as ST-Link, J-Link, or OpenOCD preferred.
* Familiarity with Linux and running Python or shell scripts preferred.
* Experience with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or serial terminals (UART, CAN), basic soldering and rework skills, and experience with test fixtures, bed-of-nails testers, or production test stations preferred.

**Physical Requirements**

* Bench work in a lab or production environment, standing or seated for long periods.
* Lift and move boxes and equipment up to 25 lb.
* Close-up visual work with small components; magnification provided.
* Use of ESD protective equipment required.

Stratom, Inc. is a mission-driven engineering company building autonomous and unmanned off-highway vehicles and related robotic systems. Our systems operate in demanding real-world environments, where performance, reliability, and engineering discipline are essential. Integrating advanced autonomy with rugged industrial hardware for austere conditions.
  
  
Our work spans the full lifecycle of complex systems, from early concept and prototyping through fielded deployment. With multiple working prototypes in hand, our next major opportunity is transitioning these platforms into production over the coming years to deliver capable systems at scale. We are looking for talented and experienced engineers who want to take ownership of hard problems and play a key role in bringing multiple platforms into production.

You will develop the vehicle control software that sits between autonomy and the physical machine on rugged robotic and ground vehicle systems, where embedded design decisions directly affect safety, reliability, testability, and field supportability.  
  
The successful candidate will own embedded subsystems from early architecture and interface definition through bring-up, testing, field deployment, and long-term maintenance. **About Us - FLI**

FieldLine Industries is a Colorado-based quantum sensing company developing and manufacturing high-sensitivity quantum magnetometers and advanced multi-sensor systems. Our technology is being applied in a wide variety of application areas including navigation in GNSS-denied environments, unexploded ordnance detection, maritime sensing, and space systems.

Our technology sits at the intersection of quantum physics, precision engineering, and real-world deployment—transforming applications in navigation, space and geographical mapping, geophysics, defense applications, and fundamental research. We’re a small, highly technical team that values solving problems together, with curiosity, rigor, reliability and humor. We are growing our engineering team and are currently hiring a mid-level Embedded Software Engineer.

**The Role**

Working directly with our lead software engineer and a multidisciplinary team of physicists and electrical and mechanical engineers, you will build the software that makes our sensors work: the firmware that runs on them, the embedded Linux systems that host them, and the tools we use to test, calibrate and deploy them.

Most of the work in front of us sits close to the hardware—Zephyr RTOS firmware on microcontrollers, embedded Linux on the systems around our sensors, and the data paths between our FPGA signal-processing chains and the rest of the system. Our sensors also fly on drones and are headed to orbit on small satellite payloads, so the same day might include writing a device driver, chasing a timing bug with a logic analyzer, and debugging telemetry from a field test. The work also reaches up the stack when we need it to: analyzing sensor data, storing and serving it, and moving it between instruments, vehicles and ground systems over the network.

This is a high-impact, high-ownership role. You will own major software subsystems, help set the engineering practices for software at FieldLine, and see your code run on hardware deployed in the field.

This role is ideal for an engineer who is most at home where software meets hardware, and who is happy to follow a problem wherever it leads—down into a register map, across into a schematic, or up into a Python script that automates the test.

We’ll be upfront: the range of work here is broad, and we don’t expect anyone to arrive knowing all of it. What we’re looking for is a solid embedded foundation in C/C++ and real hardware, plus the curiosity and self-direction to pick up the rest. * Strong C programming skills (C++ a plus) for resource-constrained, real-time systems

* Hands-on experience bringing up new hardware and debugging at the hardware/software boundary with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG/SWD debuggers

new_jobs.title: Design & Automation Engineer
new_jobs.description:
**Welcome to Lava Island**

Lava Island is an indoor play oasis where kids fly across trampolines, vanish into towering jungle gyms, dive into foam pits, and race down slides while families share pizza and celebrate birthdays in the party rooms. It is loud, bright, and full of energy.

Every trampoline, deck, slide, and play piece is made by hand. **Active Play Solutions (APS)** is the team that makes them. Before any of it gets built, somebody has to design it. That is you.

**The Job**

You will own original product design for Lava Island's playground and jump deck equipment, built in Autodesk Inventor, from first concept through build-ready specification. You will also work with the automation that makes APS's production floor smarter and more efficient as manufacturing scales.

This is a from-scratch role. You are not maintaining files somebody else built, you are the one building them, and you will lead APS's move from AutoCAD to Inventor, training the team on the new way of working as you go.

**Why APS**

* **Real design authority.** Build from concept, not from a spec somebody else already made.
* **Two disciplines, one seat.** Product design and automation both live on your desk.
* **Build something.** The CAD standards and design library for APS are being built right now. You help set how it runs.
* **Own the transition.** Lead the move to Inventor and shape how design works here going forward.
* **Denver home base.** On-site, minimal travel.
* Per company benefits program.
  

**What You Will Do**

**Design the equipment**

* Design playground and jump deck equipment from concept through build-ready specification in Autodesk Inventor.
* Review drawings and models for accuracy, manufacturability, and compliance with our design standards.
* Build a library of reusable design templates, standard parts, and design documentation for APS.

**Build the automation**

* Design and refine warehouse automation and machine programming as production volume scales.
* Evaluate and recommend equipment and tooling upgrades that improve manufacturing efficiency.

**Lead the transition**

* Move APS from AutoCAD to Inventor, building the training materials and coaching the team through it.

**Coordinate across teams**

* Work with the Design/architecture team in Revit so equipment integrates cleanly with building layouts.
* Partner with production floor leadership to refine designs based on real build feedback.

  

**What You Need**

* 5+ years in mechanical or product design, with real, original design work in Autodesk Inventor, not just editing existing files.
* Autodesk Certified Professional in Inventor for Mechanical Design (or equivalent) is strongly preferred, and matters more to us than a four-year degree. Real, demonstrated Inventor experience is what we're looking for.
* Strong working knowledge of Inventor iProperties, including their role in drawings, bills of materials, and design documentation.
* Experience integrating CAD design with automation, CNC, or robotics systems.
* Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and manufacturing requirements.
* Comfortable teaching others a new tool and new design standards.
* Comfortable working on-site in a production/warehouse environment.
* Comfort with email, digital documentation, and design/PDM systems. APS operates in a Microsoft 365 environment.

  

Background in playground, amusement, or structural steel manufacturing is a plus. So is familiarity with Revit, experience building configurable product models, experience with process automation or “smart” manufacturing systems, and having led a CAD platform transition before.

**Ready to Build What's Next?**

If you want to be the one designing what Lava Island builds next, not just running someone else's files, we want to meet you. Apply today.

### **Description**

Stratom, Inc. is a mission-driven engineering company building autonomous and unmanned off-highway vehicles and related robotic systems. Our systems operate in demanding real-world environments, where performance, reliability, and engineering discipline are essential. Integrating advanced autonomy with rugged industrial hardware for austere conditions.  
  
Our work spans the full lifecycle of complex systems, from early concept and prototyping through fielded deployment. With multiple working prototypes in hand, our next major opportunity is transitioning these platforms into production over the coming years to deliver capable systems at scale. We are looking for talented and experienced engineers who want to take ownership of hard problems and play a key role in bringing multiple platforms into production.

Stratom is seeking a Robotics Software Engineer with 3-5 years of experience to support the design, development, testing, and integration of advanced autonomus robotic systems.  
  
This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys hands-on problem solving and working across the full development process - problem definition, system design, implementation, testing, and deployment.  
  
The Robotics Software Engineer will work closely with experienced engineers and cross-functional teams to develop reliable software systems while growing technical expertise in robotics software development including perception, navigation, state estimation, and autonomous behaviors.

* Bachelor of Science in Robotics, Software, or Equivalent Engineering + 3 - 5 years experience

**Soft Skills**

* Strong problem-solving skills and engineering judgment
* Self-motivated with the ability to manage multiple priorities
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Collaborative team member with a hands-on approach
* Willingness to learn and take ownership of engineering challenges

These qualifications represent the types of experience that tend to be successful at Stratom. Ultimately, we are building a team that contributes to our mission.

**Additional Requirements**  
This position requires use of information which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and/or the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Non-U.S. persons selected must meet eligibility requirements for access to export-restricted information. The ITAR/EAR defines a U.S. person as a U.S. Citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident (i.e. 'Green Card Holder'), Political Asylee, or Refugee.  
  
While a DoD Security Clearance is not required when starting at Stratom, we require our employees maintain their eligibility to obtain one.

Stratom is a global leader in the development of unmanned ground vehicles and autonomous robotic systems that solve the most pressing real-world logistics and operational challenges for commercial and defense applications. Specializing in unmanned cargo movement, robotic refueling, robotic hazardous liquid transfer and autonomous mobile robots (AMR), the company’s military-proven tools, methods, technologies and strategic services solve the most difficult logistics and operational challenges. Whether in a safe, controlled settings or dynamic and challenging terrain, Stratom provides unique solutions to meet each customer’s specific needs. With its extensive expertise in R&D, engineering and system integration of autonomous technologies and solutions, Stratom, a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, is the go-to expert for global corporations, local businesses and government institutions.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Embedded Software Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Stratom, Inc. is a mission-driven engineering company building autonomous and unmanned off-highway vehicles and related robotic systems. Our systems operate in demanding real-world environments, where performance, reliability, and engineering discipline are essential. Integrating advanced autonomy with rugged industrial hardware for austere conditions.
  
  
Our work spans the full lifecycle of complex systems, from early concept and prototyping through fielded deployment. With multiple working prototypes in hand, our next major opportunity is transitioning these platforms into production over the coming years to deliver capable systems at scale. We are looking for talented and experienced engineers who want to take ownership of hard problems and play a key role in bringing multiple platforms into production.
  
  
**About the Role**  
This role is for a senior embedded software engineer who is comfortable working across architecture, implementation, hardware integration, and verification. You will develop the vehicle control software that sits between autonomy and the physical machine on rugged robotic and ground vehicle systems, where embedded design decisions directly affect safety, reliability, testability, and field supportability.
  
  
The successful candidate will own embedded subsystems from early architecture and interface definition through bring-up, testing, field deployment, and long-term maintenance. This includes defining task scheduling and data flow, implementing drivers and control logic on microcontroller-based targets, building the test infrastructure that proves the software works, and helping define the low-level safety mechanisms that keep autonomous vehicles in a safe state. You will work closely with the autonomy, electrical, mechanical, and systems teams, and play a key part in defining how vehicle control and autonomy work together. As Stratom moves multiple platforms from prototype to production, this role will help shape embedded software that is not only functional but also robust, verifiable, maintainable, and ready for deployment at scale.

**Duties and Responsibilities**
-------------------------------

* Design, develop, test, and maintain embedded software in C and C++ on microcontrollers running RTOS for vehicle control, actuation, sensing, and autonomous system functions
* Develop and integrate peripherals and interfaces for CAN, PWM, GPIO, SPI, I2C, UART ADC, timers, and watchdog
* Own software architecture and design decisions for embedded subsystems, and lead design and code reviews
* Define and own the runtime architecture of embedded vehicle software, including task scheduling, inter-module data flow, and diagnostics
* Build unit, integration, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and system-level tests, and integrate them into CI/CD pipelines to meet quality, repeatability, and schedule goals
* Lead embedded software bring-up on new vehicle platforms, including controller configuration, peripheral and network verification, and integration with sensors and actuato
* Triage issues and perform root cause analysis using system context, field observations, and log data
* Work with the autonomy and systems teams to define the vehicle control–autonomy interface, including messaging, fault handling, and platform safety requirements
* Contribute to the design and implementation of vehicle-level safety mechanisms for autonomous platforms, such as fault monitoring, emergency stop, and fail-safe behavior
* Mentor engineers and promote sound software and system safety practices across the team

  

**Qualifications**
------------------

**Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field
* 5+ years of professional embedded software development experience
* Strong proficiency in C and C++
* Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, static analysis, and code quality tools
* Experience with CAN and SAE J1939
* Experience developing software in a Linux environment
* Strong proficiency in Python for test automation and engineering tools
* Strong debugging, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  

  

**Preferred Skills**

* Experience designing and developing test infrastructure for safety-critical systems, including HIL/SIL environments and automated regression testing
* Familiarity with functional safety standards such as MIL-STD-882E and ISO 26262
* Experience with structured development processes, including requirements traceability, verification, and validation
* Experience designing software for multiple hardware targets, including HAL design and cross-platform build systems
* Familiarity with coding standards such as MISRA C/C++
* Hands-on experience with lab equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, CAN tools) and reading schematics
* Experience with ROS or ROS 2
* Experience with PID or vehicle control systems
* Experience deploying and supporting software across a fleet of autonomous vehicles or mobile robots

**A Note About This Role**
  
These qualifications represent the types of experience that tend to be successful at Stratom. We are intentionally building a small, highly effective team, and we value engineers who bring complementary strengths. Roles at Stratom often intersect, and the exact responsibilities may evolve based on the skills and initiative of the person who joins. Ultimately, we are building a team that contributes to our mission.

**Additional Requirements**  
This position requires use of information which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and/or the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). new_jobs.description:
This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for an **Intermediate Professional, Electrical Engineering** for our **Meridian, ID** office. Be involved in projects with our **ESSP (Electrical Studies, SCADA & Protection) Team** and be a part of a growing organization that meets our clients' objectives and solves their challenges.

WSP brings global expertise in power delivery, power generation, and program management—anchored by the acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. TRC Companies have now joined WSP, deepening our power practice and expanding our energy advisory and intelligent grid services. We're partnering with clients to shape how energy systems evolve around the world—and we need your help.

The successful applicant will be responsible for performing services related to electrical studies, SCADA, and system protection. Depending on project needs and individual expertise, this role may involve supporting a broad range of activities or specializing in a specific area as outlined under “Your Impact.” Candidates are not expected to be proficient in all listed areas, they are expected to have a fundamental understanding of three-phase power and power system fundamentals. Applicable power systems primarily include conventional and renewable generation facilities, substations, transmission systems, and distribution systems. Activities may include one or more of the following:

**Your Impact:**

* Protective Relaying: short circuit and symmetrical component analysis, time-current coordination, protection scheme and criteria development, relay settings calculation, integration with SCADA systems, NERC compliance, and arc flash analysis. Applicable software: AcSELerator Quickset (SEL-5030), AcSELerator Architect, GE EnerVista, ASPEN OneLiner, Gridscale X (CAPE), SKM-PTW, ETAP, RSCAD/RTDS
* Power System Planning Studies: steady-state real and reactive power flow including outage contingencies, generation interconnect feasibility, P-V and Q-V analysis for voltage stability margins, dynamic stability performance, automation of large batch simulations, working with models from NERC regional entities (WECC, MRO, SERC etc.), NERC compliance. Applicable Software: PSS/E, PSLF, PowerWorld, DSA Tools, Python Scripting
* Design Studies: substation grounding, corona, electric and magnetic fields, insulation coordination (lightning, switching surge, and contamination performance), transient (time domain) simulation, power quality (harmonics, voltage flicker, over/under voltage, etc.), motor starting, AC interference (transmission line interaction with railroads and pipelines). Applicable Software: CDEGS, ATP-EMTP, PSCAD, POLARIS-EMF, COMSOL Multiphysics, TFlash
* Networking and Communications: design and configure network and communication paths for Remote Terminal Units (RTUs), protective relays, meters, Human Machine Interface (HMIs), PLC’s and other SCADA system equipment; develop basic specifications for fiber optic, microwave, power line carrier, or radio communication paths; travel to project sites to troubleshoot and commission network and communication systems. Applicable network and communication protocols: DNP, Modbus, SEL Communication Protocol, Goose Messaging, IEC 61850
* Logic and Control Systems: develop and implement logic and control schemes for remote and local operation of power system equipment; develop programs on various platforms for implementation of these schemes; travel to project sites to test and commission the control schemes. Applicable Logic and Control Platforms: SEL RTAC, Orion, Cooper SMP, GE-D20
* Write technical reports summarizing analysis with findings and conclusions, generating complete, accurate, and concise documentation using sketches, calculations, electronic systems, spreadsheets, and software.
* Assist technical staff and project managers with risk identification and assessment, offering input and analysis with design concepts, construction, mitigation and improvement activities, and remediation projects.
* Assist with work plan preparation and coordination of field/site work and permitting.
* Complete training on assigned tasks.
* Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.
* Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.  

**Who You Are:**

**Required Qualifications**

* BSEE (BS Electrical Engineering), BSEET (BS Electrical Engineering Technology), or BSCE (BS Computer Engineering) degree, from an ABET-accredited university
* One 1+ years of industry experience performing design or device configuration in technical disciplines described in the Roles and Responsibilities section
* Knowledge of electrical engineering principles, practices, process, design/build, and the application to permitting and project work-related issues.
* Analytical mindset with an ability to exercise sound judgement in evaluating situations and making decisions.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to an engineering and non-engineering audience.
* Capable self-leadership with attention to detail, accuracy, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
* Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, as well as part of a team to meet business objectives.
* Basic proficiency with technical writing, office automation, software, technology, math principles, predictive models, spreadsheets, and tools.
* Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.

Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

new_jobs.description:
**Job Summary:**

This entry level/early career professional, applied science position utilizes the core competencies of thermal and fluid sciences, using and advancing analytical and experimental approaches to answer key questions about the performance and architecture of a system or component. This drives decisions and creates technical content which ultimately leads to state of the art, highly effective, environmentally friendly, and competitive products.

**Key Responsibilities:**

Investigates product, system, and/or technology problems that are related to thermal and fluid sciences, understands causal mechanisms, recommends appropriate action, owns problem resolution and documents results with guidance from more experienced team members. Applies and supports the improvement of processes such as Pre Program Planning, (PPP), Product Preceding Technology, (PPT), Value Package Introduction (VPI), or Value Package Change, (VPC), Engineering Standard Work, (ESW), Functional Excellence Practice (FEP) and tools related to thermal and fluid sciences such as GT-Suite, Boost, Fluent, Converge, Concerto, CyberApps (virtual application model), Cummins Data Analysis Tool (CDAT), Mach, test data calculation, DARTS, test data storage, Calterm, Electronic Control Module (ECM) calibration tool, Emissions data system, Integrity, and ACCEPTS ECM in-loop test bench required to support the processes and enable high quality decision making. Obtains input and negotiates with immediate stakeholders, such as team members, technical managers, project leaders, other Thermal Sciences engineers, product and manufacturing engineers, and supplier partners and delivers information and recommendations to support project decisions, or to provide input related to further analysis, design optimization, feasibility studies, or architecture definition. Makes decisions in the areas of day to day project details, such as conducting analysis, testing, and communication with stakeholders that impact and support the successful progression of projects. Owns problem resolution for moderately complex components, products, systems, subsystems or services with technical complexity and ambiguity increasing as experience is gained in the role. Provides independent execution of established work processes and systems, while still developing technology or product knowledge; engages with the improvement of systems and processes. Involves minimal direct management of people, but could involve the coordination and direction of work amongst technicians and/or temporary student employees. Contributes effectively toward team goals, exhibits influence within a work group and continues to develop proficiency in the competency areas critical to success in the role.

**Competencies:**

Applies Principles of Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer - Interprets and predicts the performance of fluid and thermal systems by leveraging a quantitative and intuitive comprehension of the flow of liquids and gases, the transfer of thermal energy between elements of a system, and the application of modeling and experimental tools, to answer key questions about the system or component.

Applies Principles of Thermodynamics and Energy Conversion Systems - Interprets and predicts the performance of energy conversion systems such as IC engines, gas turbines, fuel cells, and batteries, by leveraging a quantitative and intuitive comprehension of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, modeling tools, controls, and experimental tools to answer key questions about the system or component.

Product Failure Mode Avoidance - Mitigates potential product failure modes, by identifying interfaces, functions, functional requirements, interactions, control factors, noise factors, and prioritized potential failure modes and potential failure causes for the system of interest to effectively and efficiently improve the reliability of Cummins’ products.

Product Function Modeling, Simulation and Analysis - Impacts product design decisions through the utilization and/or interpretation of computational tools and methods that predict the capability of a product's function relative to its system, sub-system and/or component level requirements.

Product Problem Solving - Solves product problems using a process that protects the customer; determines the assignable cause; implements robust, data-based solutions; and identifies the systemic root causes and recommended actions to prevent problem reoccurrence.

System Requirements Engineering - Uses appropriate methods and tools to translate stakeholder needs into verifiable requirements to which designs are developed; establishes acceptance criteria for the system of interest through analysis, allocation and negotiation; tracks the status of requirements throughout the system lifecycle; assesses the impact of changes to system requirements on project scope, schedule, and resources; creates and maintains information linkages to related artifacts.

Systems Thinking - Defines the system of interest by drawing the boundaries, identifying its context within its environment, its interfaces, and that it has a lifecycle to aid in planning the problem statement, scope and deliverables ; analyzes linkages and interactions between elements that comprise the system of interest by using appropriate methods, models and integration of outcomes to understand the system, predict its behavior and devise modifications to it in order to produce the desired effects.

Collaborates - Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.

Communicates effectively - Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.

Decision quality - Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.

Drives results - Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.

Self-development - Actively seeking new ways to grow and be challenged

new_jobs.title: Technical Programme Manager, Electrical Engineering
new_jobs.description:
**About IonQ:**

  

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world's leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ's newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.  
  
Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

**Role Overview**
-----------------

**Role:**
---------

IonQ is building quantum computers that change which problems the world can solve. Our Control Electronics team creates every custom electronic device inside an IonQ system, taking the hardware, gateware, firmware and test behind the precision control boards around the ion trap from development through to production.

As Technical Programme Manager for Electrical Engineering, you will drive the team's workstreams, working directly with the programme lead TPM in our Programme Management Office. You will sit at the centre of a cross-functional group of engineers and physicists, turning complex technical work into clear plans, measurable milestones and predictable delivery for our quantum computing roadmap. This is a hands-on role that takes real weight off our design engineers, so they can stay focused on design and the bench.

**Responsibilities:**
---------------------

You will create and run the operating rhythm that keeps teams aligned and leaders informed: building development plans and an integrated schedule, tracking dependencies and surfacing risk early. You do not need to be the designer, but you need to be technical enough not to be fooled. When an estimate looks too long or a fix is always two days away, you will know which questions to ask, bring in the right architect or physicist, and turn the answer into a realistic plan with the right number of steps.

Much of the help the team needs sits between functions. You will be the link between design engineering, procurement, materials management, supply chain, NPI and production, organising orders, parts and boards so that engineers handle the technical questions and the logistics are handled for them. When a component has a long lead time, you will understand its key characteristics well enough to help find an alternative. You will also keep embedded software, systems architecture and physics requirements in step with the electronics plan, represent the team's progress in programme meetings so that leads do not have to attend every one, and travel up to 20% of the time to partner sites as needed.

**Key responsibilities include:**
---------------------------------

* Drive the control electronics workstreams across hardware, gateware, firmware and test, owning schedule, resources, dependencies and stakeholder alignment
* Build and maintain a realistic integrated schedule, challenging estimates and surfacing technical and schedule risk early
* Coordinate orders, parts and boards with procurement, materials management and suppliers, and help resolve long lead and obsolete component issues
* Drive cross-functional execution with physics, systems, embedded software, NPI and production teams, taking issues to closure with clear mitigation plans
* Establish programme cadences and executive reporting, including dashboards, status updates and decision logs

**Requirements:**
-----------------

We are looking for a technically fluent programme manager with genuine hardware programme experience, who brings structure, pace and precision to complex electronics work. You will have run, or worked closely inside, the full hardware lifecycle, including firmware and lower level test, from requirements and design through fabrication, bring-up and revision into production. You will have enough exposure to firmware or RTL work to judge whether an estimate is realistic, even if you have not written that code yourself.

You will bring a degree in electrical engineering or a related technical field, and an advanced degree is a plus. You will be comfortable working day to day with physicists and engineers, building trust quickly, and translating progress, risks and trade-offs into clear, decision-ready reporting for senior stakeholders. You thrive in ambiguity, can spot inconsistencies in messy data, and enjoy both sides of the job: getting into the detail of procurement and tracking, and knowing when to take a technical discussion offline with the right people.

**You'd be a great fit with:**
------------------------------

* Experience as a technical programme manager delivering complex electronics hardware programmes from development into production
* A degree in electrical engineering or a related technical field
* Working knowledge of firmware, gateware or RTL development and lower level hardware test
* Hands-on experience managing procurement, component sourcing and supplier issues for prototype or low-volume builds
* Fluency with modern programme tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet and GitHub

The total compensation package includes base salary, bonus, equity, and a range of benefits available on our career site.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office locat
